message: Plan opened for Fort npm token rotation. Scope is npm-only implementation now, with future-provider shape documented but not implemented speculatively.

Created branch feat/npm-token-rotation. Implemented fort rotate npm as a client-side Fort CLI command that reads old token, management token, and npm password through Fort, requires OTP from a 0600 file, creates a new npm token, writes it back through Fort, optionally revokes the old token, and redacts token output. Added focused unit tests and local Fort plus mock npm registry integration coverage.

Validation passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, and fort rotate npm --help. Svelta key-name inspection through si fort is blocked in this shell because no managed Codex Fort runtime session is available; do not bypass Fort by reading Safe directly.

Rechecked Svelta with CODEX_HOME=/home/shawn/.si/codex/profiles/gadolina. Fort auth works, but Fort list returns secret scope not found for svelta, svelta-blog, and svelta-docs across dev/prod/staging. Repo references show NPM_TOKEN is the Svelta publish key; svelta-docs documents a Fort-backed local publish path expecting NPM_TOKEN in safe/svelta-docs/.env.prod, but that Fort scope is absent. Local gh auth and Fort-listed orbit/prod GitHub PAT candidates return 401 Bad credentials, so GitHub Actions secret inspection/update is also blocked.

Repeated live-rotation checks still cannot proceed. Fort npm rotation implementation remains clean and mock-registry e2e passes. Svelta Fort scopes are absent for svelta, svelta-blog, and svelta-docs across dev/prod/staging. Additional Fort-listed GitHub PAT candidates in orbit/dev, orbit/prod, viva/dev, and viva/prod all return GitHub 401 Bad credentials. Live Svelta npm rotation requires external provisioning of Fort-backed Svelta npm credentials or valid GitHub credentials plus current npm OTP.

Added an optional GitHub Actions repository secret sink to fort rotate npm. The command now can update workflows that consume secrets.NPM_TOKEN by fetching the repo public key, encrypting the new npm token with GitHub-compatible sealed-box encryption, and PUTing only encrypted_value/key_id. The local e2e now covers npm create, Fort write, GitHub encrypted secret update, and old npm token revoke.

Final resumed audit: commit 13d5feb remains clean and fort_cli_rotates_npm_token_through_mock_registry passes. Fort still returns secret scope not found for svelta, svelta-blog, and svelta-docs across dev/prod/staging. GitHub auth remains invalid for all checked Fort-listed candidates in orbit/dev, orbit/prod, viva/dev, and viva/prod. No live Svelta npm rotation can be run safely until Fort-backed Svelta npm credentials or valid GitHub credentials plus npm OTP are externally provisioned.

Improved npm rotation dry-run so it validates provider config and sink shape without reading Fort secrets or contacting Fort/npm/GitHub. Verified a Svelta-shaped dry-run with an unreachable Fort host succeeds and reports secret_values_loaded=false plus the planned GitHub Actions NPM_TOKEN sink.

Followed the user clarification to inspect Safe structurally and use only si fort for credential checks. There is no safe/svelta* scope; the Svelta/Aureuma npm candidates are under safe/aureuma and exposed through Fort as aureuma/dev and aureuma/prod. aureuma/prod has NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, and SV_NPM_GAT_AUREUMA; NPM_TOKEN and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN are identical. npm rejects SV_NPM_GAT_AUREUMA in both prod and dev with E401 on npm whoami, and aureuma/prod does not expose NPM_PASSWORD/NPM_OTP, so live npm rotation remains blocked on valid npm management credentials and OTP/password input.

Adjusted `fort rotate npm` to support an optional `--password-key` path (`--password-key` omitted => create request can omit password) so managed npm tokens that permit passwordless create/revoke are supported. This is in progress while credentials remain external blockers; live Svelta rotation still awaits valid npm management/OTP and GitHub auth inputs.

Added actionable error handling when no password was supplied: if npm token create responds 400 with password-related rejection, CLI now surfaces a clear guidance message to provide --password-key for that token-management credential.

Plan updated on main after merge: scope now explicitly npm-only in production code, version bumped to 0.2.20, and provider-expansion roadmap added (GitHub, Docker Hub, cloud providers) while remaining live blockers remain credential/OTP/GitHub auth dependent.
